Nike's release shows broad channel/product weakness [E17][E34], suggesting execution rather than brand exodus; no market-share data proves a transfer.

**Bargain or trap?** Neither extreme. At $75.43 [C1], $NKE trades at 20.22x [C13] trailing earnings with a 4.42% [C19] FCF yield, and the price implies 4.19% [C35] annual FCF growth against a 0.46% [C17] four-year CAGR. The 5-year-low claim is unverifiable — the price series starts 2024-01-02 [E4]; verified are a -19.98% [C2] one-day move and -29.21% [C3] year to date. The short-window beta driving the discount rate moves the answer most. Guidance is third-party [E24], FY24 cash flow unfiled, the risk-free rate declared [A1]. Some filing-prose cells were flagged unverified — an inline digital decline, a hand-summed nine-month figure, balance-sheet amounts in millions, the return count and a few inline percentages: descriptive context only, not recomputed.
